alerts.title: Carbamazepine-DTG interaction with virologic failure
alerts.message: Guidelines state carbamazepine decreases dolutegravir levels by 30-70% and recommend using valproic acid instead. Patient takes DTG (TLD) alongside newly started carbamazepine 400 mg twice daily, and viral load rose from <50 to 1,240 copies/mL. The interaction is a plausible cause of reduced DTG exposure, though adherence is reported good and other causes were not excluded. Guidelines advise repeating VL in 2-3 months with enhanced adherence support when VL >50 copies/mL.

evidence.recommended_action: Avoid carbamazepine with DTG; use valproic acid per guidance. Repeat VL in 2-3 months, provide enhanced adherence support, and address potential side effects affecting adherence.

alerts.title: Viral load detectable: monitoring and genotype evaluation
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend action when VL exceeds 50 copies/mL on DTG-based first-line ART, including enhanced adherence support and repeat VL. Patient VL is 1,240 copies/mL, and the VL algorithm recommends genotype testing when failure is confirmed. Given possible interaction-related drug exposure loss, close virologic follow-up is needed.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat VL in 2-3 months with enhanced adherence support; if VL remains detectable, perform genotype testing per the VL testing algorithm.

alerts.title: Carbamazepine toxicity with hyponatremia and ALT rise
alerts.message: Patient presents with nystagmus, ataxia, tremor and carbamazepine level 14 mcg/mL (therapeutic 4-12), consistent with carbamazepine toxicity. Sodium is 128 mmol/L and ALT 68 U/L; carbamazepine can contribute to hyponatremia and hepatotoxicity, though valproate (also a hepatotoxic and hyponatremia-associated agent) is co-administered and was not evaluated in the excerpts. Attribution is not confirmed from the provided guideline excerpts.

evidence.recommended_action: Reduce carbamazepine dose and repeat level as planned; review sodium and liver function; consider valproate contribution and neurology input given seizure history.
